summary: Continuation of the He18 extraction with explicit integral compact-open volume, finite-sum convolution and local-unit proofs; a twisted-commutator proof without stable-subgroup assumptions; the actual rational-character apartment and finite affine kernel; and compatible Lang solutions via finite inverse systems. All earlier items, routes, source findings and central-twist/rigid-presentation repairs are preserved. Actual BT/congruence producers and the HN14 transfer remain open, so the extraction stays partial.

conventions.local: F is a nonarchimedean local field of either characteristic, residue field F_q of characteristic p; G is the F-points of a connected reductive F-group, with maximal F-split torus A, chosen alcove, Iwahori I and pro-p Iwahori I'.
conventions.coefficients: R is a commutative Z[1/p]-algebra, given the discrete topology for test functions. Haar volume is normalized by μ(I')=1. Convolution is NOT the pointwise multiplication instance on compactly supported continuous maps.
conventions.twisting: θ is an automorphism of G preserving A and I, continuous and inducing finite-order actions on the apartment and Iwahori–Weyl group. ω:G→R× has open kernel. T_x f(g)=ω(x)f(x⁻¹gθ(x)); supp(T_x f)=x supp(f) θ(x)⁻¹.
conventions.guard: The phrase finite-minima guard means that the fibre of Ω→Ω_θ over each κ under consideration is finite, for example θ=id. This is a genuine extra scope restriction on the printed finite-minimal-element argument, not an implication of finite order of θ.
conventions.scope: The corrected Howe conclusion is field-valued (characteristic different from p). C17/L18 now remove the finite-minima guard from its conditional proof, while the actual affine and filtration producers remain open. No general-ring dual finite-generation assertion is retained. Newton partition and rigid presentation retain explicit source obligations.
conventions.baseline: Library means an exact stated ingredient, not an implemented p-adic specialization. All implementationStatus values remain unchecked.

items.statement: For the fixed alcove barycenter let I_n be the integer-depth Moy–Prasad filtration, with I_0=I in the paper's convention and positive levels compact open pro-p. items.name: Separation of distinct Newton power growth
items.statement: For standard-triple cells with distinct dominant Newton vectors, no fixed g∈G θ-conjugates an element of one to the other. Assume the validated full-apartment action C2, finite-order θ on W̃, N6 and the local simple-cell adapters in N18. The proof handles Ω-cosets and central translations directly.
proofSteps: Choose n0 divisible by the order of θ on W̃, with (xiθ)^n0 acting as translation λi. If hi are conjugate by fixed g∈IżI, their n0m-fold twisted products remain conjugate by g and θ^(n0m)(g). The latter stays in IżI; θ need not have finite order on G itself.

Use N6 to bound the parabolic errors by the fixed finite groups WK1 and WK2. Move the second finite-parabolic error to the other side, using inversion. All outside cells then range over fixed finite sets independent of m.
N18 gives finite endpoint sets A,B and an equality t^(mλ2)=a_m t^(mλ1)b_m of Bruhat labels for every m; disjointness of Bruhat cells is used here. Apply their full affine actions.
N19 forces λ2 into the W0-orbit of λ1, contrary to distinct dominant Newton vectors. No inference that z∈Wa, nor positivity of length on central translations, is used.
acceptance: Distinct central translations of GL2 must be separated even though both have Coxeter length zero; the printed inequality alone cannot do so.

items.statement: For the datum of F5 with X = I = Z_2^×, evaluation at 1_I carries the invariant distributions supported on I onto Ann_R(t) = V, which is not a finitely generated R-module. items.name: Newton displacement for a possibly nonfaithful affine action
items.statement: Let phi(v)=L v+c be an affine automorphism with L of finite order d. Then phi^d is translation by lambda=sum_(i=0)^(d-1)L^i c and nu=lambda/d. This vector is independent of the annihilating power d. Affine conjugation by a map with linear part M sends nu to M nu. Finite kernels in the acting group do not affect this construction; central directions are retained.
proofSteps: Iterate the affine map to obtain the geometric sum. For every multiple kd the displacement is k lambda, so division by kd gives nu. Compare arbitrary annihilating powers through their least common multiple.
Conjugation takes a translation by lambda to one by M lambda. Apply this to the dth power.

For w theta, the linear parts lie in the finite group generated by W0 and the finite-order theta action. The average applies on the full apartment without requiring (w theta)^d to be a chosen translation in Wtilde itself.

gaps.detail: Theorem 4 (every element reduces to a minimal length element), Theorem 6 (π is a bijection on straight classes), Theorem 7 with Remark 8 (the standard triple) and [16, Corollary 2.8] (a minimal element with central Newton point lies in W_Pτ) are imported from He–Nie, and their proofs — the Newton axis, the gradient descent to an axis alcove, the finite-parabolic partial conjugation and the axis-alcove factorisation — are not given here. A design job plans them from He–Nie, together with the partial-conjugation results of He that their Theorem 2.5 cites; items C13–C16 record what has to be planned.

gaps.title: The Newton separation argument
gaps.detail: The proof of Theorem 3 in §2.6 has the two defects recorded as findings E7 and E11 (the elements y, y′ run over W̃, not W_a; θ^{nl} for θ^{n_0l}), and one step it does not justify: the final chain ends with 2N_0 + 2♯(W_0) < l ⩽ ℓ(t^{l(λ_2−y_0λ_1)}), which needs λ_2 − y_0λ_1 to be non-central, since ℓ(t^μ) = 0 for a nonzero central μ — for instance μ = (1,1) in GL_2 — while the paper only observes λ_2 − y_0λ_1 ≠ 0. The missing step is the standard compatibility between the Kottwitz invariant and the central component of the Newton point: ν_1 and ν_2 have the same Ω_θ-factor, which fixes that component, so the difference of the Newton points is non-central. Items N18 and N19 carry the repaired comparison.

gaps.title: Lang's theorem and the Frobenius-equivariant counting
gaps.detail: Finding E5: the lifting of σ-fixed cosets in Lemma 15 and the level-n counting in Lemma 16 need the relevant congruence intersections to be k̄-points of connected pro-unipotent groups, so that Lang's theorem applies, and need the root-filtration decompositions to be σ-equivariant. Items L19–L23 supply finite-type Lang surjectivity, the finite solution torsors, the compatible solutions in the inverse limit and the fixed-coset consequence; what a design job must still construct is the connected Frobenius-equivariant model of Ĭ_n ∩ gĬ_ng^{-1} and the depth-shifted root counts. The referees of the paper had already found a mistake in an earlier version of this proof, which is recorded in its acknowledgements.

gaps.title: The twisted finiteness hypothesis, and the compact core that replaces it
gaps.detail: Finding E1: for θ ≠ id with Ω infinite — the GL_n twisted-endoscopy case the paper is written for, and G_m with inversion — a θ-twisted conjugacy class meets infinitely many W_a-cosets, so Corollary 9 fails and X_ν is not compact. Every statement that needs a compact core (Theorem A, Theorem C(2), the bound of Theorem 20) must therefore either carry the hypothesis that (1 − θ)Ω is finite — automatic for θ = id and for Ω finite, hence for G semisimple — or use the replacement this extraction records: by C17 every minimal element of a Newton fibre is θ-conjugate by an element of Ω into one chosen Ω-coset, and N20 shows the resulting core Y(ν,τ_0) is compact open with G ·_θ Y(ν,τ_0) = G(ν). A design job plans the replacement, not the printed claim.

gaps.title: Coefficients: where a field is needed and where duals may be used
gaps.detail: Findings E2, E3 and E6 all come from the same place: the paper works over an arbitrary commutative Z[1/p]-algebra R, deliberately, but the distribution arguments use duality as if R were a field. A design job must plan (i) the indexing objects as products, not direct sums (E2); (ii) the finiteness of Theorem 20 and of Howe's conjecture over a field of characteristic ≠ p, with the general-R statement only as 'a submodule of a free module of rank N_ν[I : I_n]' (E3, and item F6 for the counterexample); and (iii) the kernel of Theorem 23 by a direct computation with compactly supported test functions and arbitrary target modules (E6, items R12–R17), since Hom_{Z[1/p]}(Z[1/p]/ℓ, Z[1/p]) = 0 makes the dual argument unavailable.

gaps.title: Algebraic-group suppliers for the Lang argument
gaps.detail: The finite-field Lang surjectivity imported in L19 rests on the existence of a closed orbit and on the orbit-dimension formula (Humphreys 8.3 and 4.1), on the geometric irreducibility of a connected smooth group and on a faithful linear embedding. These are quoted, not planned here; a design job takes them from the upstream algebraic-group layers rather than restating them.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.1(a), p. 9, with Corollary 9, p. 12, Theorem A/§0.3, p. 3, and §5.2, p. 20 (both versions)
sourceIssues.printed: (a) Each θ-twisted conjugacy class of W̃ intersects only finitely many W_a cosets. [Justified by: 'Since the action of θ on V is of finite order, each θ-orbit on Ω is a finite set.']
sourceIssues.correction: The statement needs a hypothesis: that (1 − θ)Ω is finite — equivalently, that the fibres of Ω → Ω_θ are finite. It holds automatically for θ = id and whenever Ω is finite (for instance G semisimple), but not in general.
sourceIssues.reason: The image in W̃/W_a ≅ Ω of the θ-twisted conjugacy class of w′ is κ(w′) + (1 − θ)Ω, not the θ-orbit of κ(w′), because w ·_θ w′ = w w′ θ(w)^{-1} changes the W_a-coset by ω − θ(ω). Two instances. (i) G = G_m and θ inversion: W̃ = Ω = Z, W_a = 1, all lengths are 0, twisted conjugation sends m to m + 2k, so each of the two classes 2Z and 1 + 2Z meets infinitely many W_a-cosets; every element is of minimal length in its class, so Corollary 9 fails and X_ν is the set of elements of F^× of a fixed parity of valuation, which is not compact. (ii) The case the paper is written for: G = GL_n with the twisted-endoscopy automorphism g ↦ J·(ᵗg)^{-1}·J^{-1} that preserves the standard Iwahori. Then Ω ≅ Z through the valuation of the determinant, θ acts on it by −1, and the twisted class of 1 contains τ^{2k} for every k, where τ generates Ω; all of these have length 0, hence are of minimal length, and all have the same invariants π = (0,0). So again Corollary 9 and the compactness of X_ν fail. The Newton decomposition of Theorem 3 itself is unaffected, and the compactness can be restored by replacing X_ν with a compact core inside one chosen Ω-coset, which the items of this extraction do (see C17 and N20): every minimal element of a Newton fibre is θ-conjugate by an element of Ω into that coset.

review.reason: Confirmed. Page 9 prints 'Since the action of θ on V is of finite order, each θ-orbit on Ω is a finite set. Therefore (a) Each θ-twisted conjugacy class of W̃ intersects only finitely many W_a cosets.' The image in Ω = W̃/W_a of the θ-twisted class of w is not a θ-orbit but the coset [w] + (1 − θ)Ω, since Ω is abelian and [xwθ(x)^{-1}] = [w] + (1 − θ)[x]. That set is finite exactly when (1 − θ)Ω is finite, which is the hypothesis the correction adds; finiteness of the θ-orbits does not give it, as Ω = Z² with θ swapping the factors shows, where (1 − θ)Ω is infinite while every θ-orbit has at most two elements.
